name.description:
Installed-title name, joined from app.db by the payload. Absent
when the title is no longer installed -- play time outlives the
game. Every field here is `serde(default)`, so a payload that
spells a key differently reads as a default rather than an error;
the payload's activity_json selftest pins the wire spellings.

ActivityResetResult.description: Result of resetting recorded play time.

AddRepo.description: What a repo is added with.

read_only.description: `true`: agents can only look. `false`: they can change things too.

locked.description:
`PS5UPLOAD_MCP_READ_ONLY` in the engine's environment holds it read-only, whatever the
switch says.

read_only.description: In force now: agents can only look.

setting.description: The app's switch ("Agents can change things" is its opposite).

confirm.description: The person said yes in the UI. Without it the engine does nothing.

kind.description: `folder`: added to the game's own folder. `backport`: a backport folder for an image.

rescanned.description: Whether ShadowMount+ was asked to scan again (a console's image only).

source.description: A game folder on this computer, or on a console (`ps5://<ip>/<path>`).

block_kib.description: The block size in KiB, a power of two from 16 to 1024; 64 when absent.

install_runtime.description:
Put ampr_emu 0.4.2.1 into the image's `fakelib/libSceAmpr.sprx` (the game's own kept
as `.orig`) when the game ships none or one that predates asset packs.

profile_toml.description: A profile in drakmor's `ampr_pack` TOML format, used in place of the built-in one.

runtime.description:
Which ampr-emu-ng goes in: `latest` (the default: the newest GitHub release, used only
when its download matches the SHA-256 GitHub publishes for it, else the tested one) or
`pinned` (the tested release). The job's `commit_ack.ampr_runtime` says which went in.

offset.description:
One page's window (#473): the first row it holds, the row the next page starts at, and
whether one follows. Absent from an older helper, which answers one unpaged reply, and
from the list [`appdb_query`] returns, which is every page joined.

source.description:
Which reader answered: `sqlite`, `sqlite-immutable` or `scan`.

Worth surfacing rather than hiding. `scan` means the SQL open
failed and the rows came from the byte-level b-tree reader, which
recovers title ids reliably but display names only sometimes — so
a caller that sees a blank name knows whether to believe it.

total.description:
The table's row count when the page was read (SQL reader only). A change between pages
means rows moved under the walk, so one may have been skipped: the list is truncated.

truncated.description:
True when app.db holds rows this list does not: the helper could not deliver them, a
page failed (`err` says why), the page bound was reached, or an older helper answered
a full 256 rows (its old cap, which it could not report). A truncated list is never
proof that a title is absent.

AppDumpResult.description:
What [`app_dump`] wrote. `decrypt_skipped` is empty, or why no file was decrypted (the
payload's token, e.g. `dump_decrypt_unsupported_fw`); `fw` is the console's firmware as
hex (`0x13600000`), empty when it could not be read.

AppInfoRow.description: One (key, value) row of appinfo.db for a title.

AppLaunchReq.description:
Launch a registered title via the payload's triple-strategy
`sceLncUtilLaunchApp` → `sceSystemServiceLaunchApp` flow. Title
must already be registered in app.db (we surface the existing
`register_title_*` flow elsewhere). Re-exposed in 2.2.26 after
previously being gated out of the UI.

AppRegisterReq.description:
Stage + register a PS5 game folder so Sony's launcher picks it up
in the XMB. `src_path` may live on /data, /mnt/ext*, /mnt/usb*, or
inside a mounted /mnt/ps5upload/ image. Idempotent: re-registering
the same path is a no-op (Sony's installer returns 0x80990002,
which the payload normalises). Re-exposed in 2.2.26 — engine core
and payload were already wired but the HTTP/Tauri layer hadn't
been opened up.

patch_drm_type.description:
2.2.26 opt-in: rewrite `<src>/sce_sys/param.json`'s
`applicationDrmType` to `"standard"` before staging. Default
false (don't touch the user's source).

AppState.description:
Scheduler-visible state of one running app.

This is the part that actually answers "is the game on screen?" on a
firmware with no focus getter. A PS5 game that loses the screen is
suspended or has its CPU budget collapsed, so `runtime_us` sampled over
time separates foreground from background behaviourally — no Sony focus
API, no crash risk, no firmware dependency.

runtime_us.description: Accumulated CPU microseconds. The rate of change is the signal.

stat.description:
FreeBSD process state. 4 == SSTOP: outright stopped, the strong
"definitely not running" signal.

AppUnregisterReq.description:
Reverse of `app_register`, and the uninstall of a package install. A
Sony refusal is an error (502) from a 7.1.6 helper; from an older one it is
`sony_uninstall_refused` in an `ok` reply, which the client must check
(#476). `still_present` says the title's folders were still there after
Sony accepted (`null` from an older helper).

device.description: OS device the image is attached to (`/dev/disk4`, `/dev/loop0`).

image.description: Absolute path of the image file.

mount_point.description:
Where the OS mounted it, when it did. Empty when the image
attached but no filesystem was mounted -- which is a real state,
not a failure: an unformatted or unsupported image attaches fine
and mounts nothing.

Autoload.description:
Payload Manager's boot autoload: on/off, the seconds it waits after boot,
and the ordered list (`/data/pldmgr/autoload.txt`, one entry a line). An
entry is a slot (`local/<leaf>`, `repo/<…>`, 0.6), a file name it matches
against its stored files, an absolute path under its folders, or `!<ms>`
for a pause. Nothing loads at boot while `enabled` is false.

AvatarApplied.description: Result of an avatar apply: which user it landed on + how many files.

dir.description: A folder on the computer the engine runs on; the backup is a new folder inside it.

stamp.description: `YYYY-MM-DD_HHMMSS` (UTC for backups the engine made), `_snap` after it for a snapshot.

tag.description: `snap`: taken while the game ran. None: an automatic (or before-restore) backup.

BackupUser.description: A user on the console when the backup was made, for matching them to a user on a reset console.

dir.description: The folder inside it to list; the root when absent.

path.description: The image or package, on this computer.

compressed.description: A `.ffpfsc`: the image sits in a compressed container.

dir.description: The folder listed, normalized ("" at the root).

editable.description: An edited copy can be written (every image kind but a package).

filesystem.description: `exfat`, `ufs2`, `pfs` or `pkg`: the filesystem inside (a `.ffpfsc`'s inner one).

label.description: The reader's one-line description of the image.

BugBundleEntry.description:
One entry to place in the bundle. Exactly one of `text` / `base64` is used;
`text` wins when both are present.

path.description: Zip-relative path, e.g. "logs/app.jsonl". Traversal is rejected.

shipped_by.description:
Ids of the sets shipping this exact build. The only signal with evidence
behind it when choosing between builds of one name.

compression.description: `fast`, `balanced` (the default) or `smallest`: how hard the Kraken encoder works.

firmware.description:
Rewrites `requiredSystemSoftwareVersion` (a BCD hex word, e.g. `0x0510000000000000` for
5.10). A console older than the declared minimum refuses the install with `0x80a3000d`.

full_verify.description:
Read the whole package back to verify it. Off (the default): the structure is checked
in full and a seeded sample of the data blocks.

keep_both.description:
When the package's name is taken in the output folder, name it `<stem> (2).pkg` (and so
on) instead of refusing: Convert's "Save each next to its source", where the folder is
the user's own and may hold anything.

language.description: A PlayGo language code (`fr-FR`, …) the package declares as its only one.

name.description: Output file stem; the content id by default.

update.description:
A PS4 update to merge into the PS4 game `source` first (`ps5upload_fpkg::ps4_merge`):
the package is the game at the update's version.

path.description: One copy's check; every queued and running check when absent.

backend.description: The helper's backend: "stub" when it makes no devices.

companion.description:
The on-console keyboard & mouse process (`ps5u-vinput`): `idle`, `starting`, `running`,
`stopped` (being started again) or `unavailable`. Absent from helpers without one.

open.description: A session is open (this engine's or another's).

applied.description:
What happened to this switched-on cheat in the running game (#627): "applied",
"waiting" (the game is not ready yet), "failed" or "changed" (the game changed it, so it
was left alone). Absent when the game is not running or the cheat is off, and from helpers
before 10.7.2.

applied_after_ms.description:
For "applied" by the helper on its own: how many ms after the game started it landed.
Absent when the helper did not see the game start, when it was switched on by hand, and
from helpers before 10.7.6.

applied_late.description:
It landed late (more than ~3 s after the game started, or the start was not seen): a patch
the game only reads at start may have come too late, and the game has to be restarted with
it on (#627).

format.description: "xml" for an XML game patch entry; absent for the other formats.

other_version.description: An XML game patch entry made for another game version than the installed one.

CheatRepo.description: Description of a community GitHub cheat repository.

content_base.description:
Base URL holding the `json/`, `shn/` and `mc4/` subdirectories.
Usually equal to `raw_base`, but repos that nest their cheats
(e.g. under `cheats/`) point this deeper.

index_files.description:
Index files in the repo root (e.g. `json.txt`, `shn.txt`).
Empty when the repo publishes no index and must be enumerated
through `tree_api` instead.

raw_base.description:
Base URL for raw file access, e.g.
`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etaHEN/PS5_Cheats/main/`

tree_api.description:
GitHub git-trees API URL used to enumerate repos that ship no
index files. Empty means "use `index_files`".

tree_prefix.description:
Path prefix inside the tree that contains the format
subdirectories, e.g. `cheats/`. Empty means the tree root.

CheatRepoEntry.description: One entry parsed from a repo index file (`filename=game_title`).

game_version.description:
Game version the cheat was authored against (`01.05`), parsed from the
same filename. Empty when absent. Cheats are version-specific, so this
is the difference between "a cheat for this game" and "a cheat that
will work".

repo_id.description: Repo ID this entry came from.

title_id.description:
Title id parsed out of the filename (`CUSA09193_01.05_2.json` →
`CUSA09193`). Empty when the name does not follow the convention.

enabled.description: How many of its cheats are switched on (saved state).

formats.description: Formats present on the console for this title (`json`, `shn`, `mc4`).

version.description:
Game version the on-console cheat targets, parsed from its filename
by the payload. Without this field serde dropped it and the client
never saw it.

truncated.description: The console stopped adding titles at its reply ceiling: the list is valid but partial.

held.description:
The helper paused the running game's cheats: it closed right after they were applied
(#550). Helpers before 9.5.0 never send it.

Check.description: One readiness finding: what was checked, whether it holds, and what was seen.

helper.description: The file is a ps5upload helper: sending it stops the helper that runs now.

CheckoutState.description:
One image checked out for editing. At most one is active at a time —
a second concurrent checkout would need a second journal and buys nothing,
since editing is a foreground activity.

mount_point.description: Where it is mounted read-write for editing.

original_path.description: Where it must be put back for SMP to pick it up again.

staged_path.description: Where the image lives *right now* (inside the staging dir).

started_at_ms.description:
Unix ms when the checkout started, so the UI can say how long a
recovered session has been open.

title_id.description: Best-effort title id, for the UI. Empty when unknown.

CompanionStatus.description: One row per companion. `error` is the reason it is not reachable.

at_ms.description: When the check started, Unix ms.

cached_verdict.description: A failure remembered from a moment ago answered; nothing reached the console.

handshake_ms.description: Opening a new session: the TCP connect, the AVA1 handshake and the pairing check.

path.description:
How the console was reached: `lan`, `tailnet_direct`, `tailnet_relayed` or
`tailnet_system` (set by the engine).

reason.description:
The failure's token (`console_rest_mode`, `ava1_unreachable`, ...), or its text when it
has none.

reused_session.description:
A live session was already pooled, so nothing was opened. Absent when a remembered
failure answered before a session was asked for.

stale_session_dropped.description:
A pooled session had stopped answering and was dropped (then opened again, or the
console was found gone).

tcp_ms.description:
A plain TCP connect to the helper's port: the quick look past a remembered failure, or
the check that a quiet session's console still answers.

tcp_ok.description: Whether that TCP connect was taken.

version.description: The helper's version from the reply.

from_root.description:
SFTP and FTP: paths are the server's own, from its `/` (as an SSH or FTP client shows
them), so the start folder and browsing can be anywhere the account may read. Off (every
connection saved before 9.11, which the missing field reads as): paths are under the
folder the server signs in to, so `/` is that folder and nothing above it is reachable.
Links saved under those paths stay valid only while it is off.

host_key.description: SFTP: the host-key fingerprint the user accepted ("SHA256:…").

insecure_tls.description:
WebDAV over HTTPS: accept the server's certificate without verifying it (a NAS with a
self-signed certificate). Never a default.

share.description: SMB only: the share the paths live in.

id.description: Editing a saved connection: a form without a new secret borrows the saved one.

insecure_tls.description: WebDAV over HTTPS: accept a self-signed certificate.

ConsoleEntry.description: One console's side of the game.

ConsoleIn.description: One console in `PUT /api/consoles`. No Debug: it can carry keys.

notes.description: Left out keeps the notes; an empty string clears them.

ConsolePort.description: One port held on the console (`net.ports`).

name.description: What usually listens there, when the port is a well-known one; a guess by number only.

scope.description:
`all` (reachable from the network), `console` (127.0.0.1 only), `lan` (the LAN address
only: most often an outgoing connection) or `busy` (held; where was not checked).

web.description:
For a well-known port, whether it serves a web page. `false` keeps the app from pointing
a browser at a loader or the helper (a stray HTTP request is not what they expect).

host.description: The console, as the other install routes name it (`host` or `host:port`).

path.description: Absolute path of a package already on the console.

from.description: The console the save is on.

from_path.description: The save folder on `from` (from the saves list).

to_path.description: An emulator's save: the folder on `to`. Left out, the same path.

to_user.description: A PS5 save: the user there. An emulator's: who the folder there belongs to.

hub.description: The home folder on the console, or (with `hub_name`) the folder to make it in.

hub_name.description: Make a new folder of this name inside `hub`.

password.description: A password other devices type to join (none: anyone on the network joins).

path.description: This device's folder: required, the user chooses it.

CropPosition.description: Position within the available crop travel; 50 centers the image.

DdpStatus.description: What a console said about itself.

code.description:
200 = awake, 620 = standby. Kept raw so an unknown code is reported
rather than flattened into a guess.

host_id.description:
The console's MAC without separators. A caller with this never needs to
ask the console for its MAC by another route.

DestinationInput.description: What an add or change asks for.

key.description: Absent on a change: keep the saved key.

preset.description: Absent on a change: the saved one (the client sends only what changes: `{"enabled":false}`).

DirEntry.description:
One directory entry returned by `list_dir`.

`kind` is one of `"file"`, `"dir"`, `"link"`, `"other"`, or `"unknown"`
(for entries whose `lstat` on the payload side failed). Size is 0 for
non-regular-file kinds. `mtime` is Unix seconds and defaults to 0 when an
older payload omits it or `lstat` failed.

DirListing.description:
A paginated directory listing response.

`total_scanned` is the number of entries `readdir` returned (before
slicing by `offset`/`limit`); clients use this to detect the natural
end of the directory vs being paginated into submission by a small
`limit`. `truncated` is set when the response buffer filled up before
the limit was reached — uncommon in practice (response body fits 256
entries), but covers the pathological "many very long filenames" case.

DiscoverResult.description: The result, shaped the way the Connection screen has always read it.

mdns.description: False when this build has no mDNS, or it could not start: only a sweep ran.

swept.description: The /24 networks swept, as `a.b.c.0/24`. Empty when mDNS already found a running helper.

DiscoveredHost.description: One row in the discovery result.

all_ips.description: All addresses seen for this host.

hostname.description: Hostname from the mDNS records, when there were any.

ip.description: Best IP to type into the host field (`pick_best_ip`).

payload_port_open.description: :9120 reachable: our payload is already running.

services.description: Service types this host advertised, without the trailing `.local.`.

DoctorFacts.description: Everything the doctor asks of the engine.

bridged_without_pin.description: A container on a bridge network with no `PS5UPLOAD_PKG_HOST_IP` pin.

console.description: The console's link, from its helper.

host.description: This computer's link toward the console (in a container: the container's own).

reply_ms.description: Middle of the connection-open times to the console, in milliseconds.

dest_dir.description: Directory to download into. Defaults to `~/Downloads/ps5upload`.

existing.description:
What to do with a different file already under the final name (the 409 below):
`resume` treats it as an earlier unfinished download of this link (it becomes the
`.partial`, whose tail is checked against the link before any byte is kept),
`replace` deletes it and downloads afresh. Absent: refuse, as before.

insecure_tls.description:
Skip TLS verification for THIS download. Same meaning as the streaming
path: it governs only what this computer accepts, never the console.

keep_name.description:
Keep the name the link gives the file. Off (the default) for a package, whose local
file must end in `.pkg` to be installed; on for an archive part, whose name is how the
parts of a set find each other (`game.part2.rar`).

DriveSensor.description:
One physical disk discovered on `/dev/daN`. Temp and usage fields are
optional because not all drives support LOG SENSE and not all are
mounted. `access_denied` is surfaced when the device node exists but
the payload can't open it (rare, only seen on very locked-down FW).

host.description:
op `remember`: a console's LAN address and its tailnet address (what "Put this PS5 on
Tailscale" records by itself). op `test_path`: the console.

name.description: op `remember`: the console's name on the tailnet (optional).

secs.description: op `test_path`: how long, 0 to end it.

Error.description: Every failure of an /api/ route. Some routes add their own fields beside these (`reason`, `field`, `op_id`).

code.description: A short snake_case name. Added from the status when a route gave none: 404 is not_found.

Estimate.description: One compression level's estimated package size and build time.

output_dir.description: Where the package would go: its drive's write speed is part of the time.

Estimates.description: What each level would cost for one game, for the Convert screen's tiles.

rates.description: What the times were worked out from, for a bug report when one is far off.

add_ampr_emu.description:
Add ampr_emu to a game that reads through libSceAmpr and ships no emulator: without one
it fails to start from an image. On unless turned off.

ampr_lz4.description: Pack the game's files into AMPR LZ4 asset packs first (exFAT only, not with `compress`).

ampr_zstd.description:
Pack the game's files into zstd asset packs for ampr-emu-ng, which goes in the image: a
plain image of any format, not with LZ4 packs. A game in LZ4 packs is decoded on the way.

compress.description: Write the image straight into a `.ffpfsc` container (no uncompressed copy on disk).

destination.description:
Where the image goes: `{"kind":"local"}` (the default: `output_dir` on this computer) or
`{"kind":"console","addr":…,"dir":…}`: straight into that PS5's folder `dir` over AVA1,
sent as it is written, so the image is never stored on this computer. The job's `dest` is
then the image's path on the PS5, and the read-back runs there. For `.exfat`, `.ffpkg`
and `.ffpfs` images, and `.exfat` with `ampr_zstd` packs; a `.ffpfsc` (`compress`), LZ4
packs and edited copies are refused for it.

edits.description:
Write an edited COPY of the image `source` (#479): its files with these changes, as an
image of the same kind (format and compression are the source's; `format`/`compress`
are ignored), named `<name>-edited` and put next to it unless `name`/`output_dir` say
otherwise. The source image is only read.

ffpfsc_level.description: How hard a `.ffpfsc` is compressed: `fast`, `balanced` (the default) or `smallest`.

format.description:
`exfat` (the default), `ffpkg` (UFS2, what ShadowMountPlus recommends) or `ffpfs`
(PFS, experimental in ShadowMountPlus 1.7).

full_verify.description:
Read every byte of the image back to verify it. Off (the default): names, sizes and
folders are checked in full and a seeded sample of the data.

keep_both.description:
When the image's name is taken in the output folder, add ` (2)` (and so on) instead of
refusing (see `BuildReq::keep_both`).

name.description:
What to call the image instead of the source's own name: a game unpacked from an
archive is named after the archive (its unpack folder's name means nothing).

output_dir.description: Where the image goes; the converter's output folder by default.

rebuild_ampr_index.description:
An edited copy of the image `source` whose one change is a regenerated
`ampr_emu.index` (Workshop's "Rebuild AMPR index", #621): written like an edited copy,
refused for a compressed image or a game that does not read through libSceAmpr.

source.description: A game folder on this computer (one with `sce_sys` in it).

update.description:
A PS4 update (a package, image or folder) merged into the PS4 game `source`: the image
is the game at the update's version (`ps5upload_fpkg::ps4_merge`). Not with `edits`.

verify_chunk_kib.description:
How much of a file the read-back check reads per call, in KiB (1024 to 65536); 8192
when absent, which measured fastest.

ExternalPkg.description: One `.pkg` found on a connected external/USB drive.

content_id.description:
ContentID from the fast outer-header read (empty for FIH until the
embedded CNT is lazily read, or for otherwise unreadable headers).

drive.description: The drive mount this was found under (`/mnt/usb0`, `/mnt/ext1`).

path.description:
Absolute on-console path, e.g. `/mnt/usb0/games/foo.pkg`. This is a
local PS5 path, so install runs straight through the normal
install-from-path cascade — no upload/staging needed.

title_id.description: Title id (CUSA…/PPSA…) derived from the content id.

path.description: The game path an unpack reported, or its unpack folder.

source.description: A `.zip`, `.7z` or `.rar` (the first volume of a multi-part set).

dest_dir.description: Local directory to write into. Created if missing.

inner_path.description:
Slash-separated path inside the image. Empty string = whole
image (the root directory).

reapply_sec.description:
Optional fan reapply interval in seconds (1–300). When present,
the payload updates the watcher thread's tick interval AND
persists it to fan_reapply.conf. Absent = leave interval unchanged.

FfpkgExtractResult.description:
Result of an extract op — caller can render "wrote N files,
total Y bytes" + per-file detail.

bytes_written.description: Total bytes written across all files.

sample_paths.description:
First N files we wrote, for renderer display. Capped to keep
the response payload small even on bulk extracts.

FfpkgInspection.description:
Inspect a local UFS2 image (.ffpkg etc) — open the superblock,
resolve sce_sys/param.sfo if present, and return a digest the UI
can render before any upload.

Lives here (not in `ufs2`) because the param.sfo parse re-uses
the same logic as the PKG inspector below — keeping them in one
crate means there's one source of truth for "what does PS5
metadata look like."

has_sce_sys.description: True when sce_sys/param.sfo was found and parsed cleanly.

image_bytes.description: Image total bytes per the superblock (block_size × block_count).

root_entries.description:
Top-level entries (one level deep). Lets the UI show "this
image contains: eboot.bin, sce_sys/, sce_module/, etc."

volume_name.description: Volume label from the superblock. Usually empty for PS5.

FileRow.description: One row of the Files tab: a package entry or a file of a folder or image.

encrypted.description: A package entry sealed with keys this app never has.

truncated.description: More rows existed than a list shows.

off.description: Stop Finder writing `.DS_Store` on network shares and USB drives (true), or let it again.

FixAction.description:
A repair the engine can perform. A closed enum rather than a
command string: the UI asks for a named action, so it cannot ask
the engine to run something arbitrary.

changed.description: What was actually done, itemised. Empty on failure.

FixedStorageEntry.description:
A fixed-storage partition entry (internal SSD, M.2) returned alongside
the hot-pluggable drives. No temperature here — the internal SSD temp
is already surfaced via the SoC sensor channels.

apis.description:
Symbol name -> whether it resolved on this firmware.

A map rather than fixed fields: the payload probes a table of
candidate names, and which ones exist varies per firmware. Measured
on FW 9.60, `sceSystemServiceGetAppIdOfBigApp` does NOT resolve.

apps.description: Every running app with a non-zero app id, with its scheduler state.

big_app_id.description: App id of the full-screen foreground app, or 0/negative when none.

focus_app_id.description:
App id of the application that currently OWNS THE SCREEN, read from
the `SceShellCoreUtilAppFocus` named event flag; -1 when unavailable.

This is the authoritative answer on a firmware that exports no focus
getter. Confirmed on FW 9.60: 0x6018 with the game on screen, 0x0007
(SceShellUI) with the dashboard up.

focus_available.description: Whether the focus flag could be opened and polled at all.

focus_rc.description: Raw return code from the flag poll, for diagnosing a failed read.

mini_app_id.description: App id of the overlaid system UI, when one is up.

monotonic_ms.description:
Payload-side CLOCK_MONOTONIC millis, so a poller can spot a gap
(helper restarted, console slept) instead of reading a stalled
value as a steady one.

Folder.description: A folder of a group, with what the scan measured.

ampr_zstd.description:
Write the game with its files in zstd asset packs for ampr-emu-ng, as an image build's
`ampr_zstd` does, as a plain folder: the packs, the files that stay loose, and the
emulator in `fakelib/libSceAmpr.sprx`. The source may then also be a game folder (on
this computer, a saved server or a console). Not with `entry`.

destination.description:
Where the folder goes: `{"kind":"local"}` (the default: `output_dir` on this computer)
or `{"kind":"server","source_id":…,"dir":…}`: a folder on a saved server, every file
written under a temporary name and renamed, the files a game starts from (`eboot.bin`,
`sce_sys/param.json`) last and only once the folder reads back there. Not with `entry`;
a console is not a destination here.

entry.description:
Save only this file or folder of the image (#479, the image browser's Save), by its
path inside the image: a folder becomes a folder named after it, a file a file. Its
name is the entry's own unless `name` says otherwise.

full_verify.description: Compare every file by SHA-256. Off (the default): every size, and a seeded sample.

keep_both.description:
When the folder's name is taken in the output folder, add ` (2)` (and so on) instead of
refusing (see `BuildReq::keep_both`).

name.description: The folder's name; the source file's name without its extension when absent.

source.description:
A game image (`.exfat`, `.ffpkg`/`.ufs2`, `.ffpfs`, `.ffpfsc`) or a debug-key `.pkg`,
on this computer, a saved server (`remote://`) or a console (`ps5://`).

update.description:
A PS4 update merged into the PS4 game `source`, as an image build's `update`; the game
may then also be a folder. Not with `entry`.

FolderCheck.description: What a folder choice would mean, for the app to show before anything is made.

detail.description: The other drive's name, or the system's words.

files.description: Files already in it (they join the drive), counted up to COUNT_LIMIT.

marker.description: It already holds a Mesh Drive marker (a drive's folder before, or this drive's).

ok.description: It can be used as chosen.

problem.description:
Why it cannot be used: bad_name, not_absolute, no_parent, not_folder, exists (a new
folder's name is taken), taken (another drive's folder), inside / holds (inside, or holding,
another drive's folder), app_data, not_writable, unreadable.

will_create.description: It does not exist yet and will be made.

application_category_type.description:
`applicationCategoryType` from param.json (0 = game, other values
are patches / vouchers / special categories).

file_count.description: File count under `path` (regular files only, not dirs / symlinks).

icon0_path.description:
Absolute path to `sce_sys/icon0.png` if present. UI renders via
Tauri's asset:// protocol.

path.description: Absolute path to the folder that was inspected.

skipped_paths.description:
Paths that couldn't be read during the walk (permission denied,
I/O error, etc.). When non-empty, `total_size` and `file_count`
reflect only what could be inspected — the UI should surface a
"partial inspection" note so the user doesn't pick a destination
drive based on an under-reported size.

title.description:
Title from param.json `localizedParameters.{defaultLanguage}.titleName`
(or any locale we can find if defaultLanguage is missing).

total_size.description: Total size across all files under `path`, in bytes.

mode.description:
Octal string like "0777". String (not u32) so JSON parsers
don't coerce to decimal and change the meaning.

mount_point.description:
Optional full mount path. New in 2.2.25 — when provided, the
payload mounts at this exact path instead of the legacy
`/mnt/ps5upload/<name>/` location. Mutually exclusive with
`mount_name`; payload prefers `mount_point` if both arrive.

read_only.description: Mount the image read-only. New in 2.2.26. Default false (RW).

op_id.description:
Optional unique 64-bit identifier the client generates so it
can poll progress (`/api/ps5/fs/op-status`) and cancel
(`/api/ps5/fs/op-cancel`) the in-flight copy. The engine
stamps this into the FS_COPY frame's trace_id so the payload's
in-flight ops table is keyed on it. Pass 0 (or omit) when no
progress/cancel is needed; the operation runs the same way
the old endpoint did.

overwrite.description:
Merge into an existing destination instead of refusing it. Files that
collide are replaced; anything already in the destination that the
source doesn't mention is left alone. Absent = an existing destination
is refused (`fs_move_exists` / `fs_copy_dest_exists`, 409 on a move), so
only a caller that has actually asked the user gets the destructive path.

FsOpCancelReq.description:
POST /api/ps5/fs/op-cancel — body `{"op_id": N, "addr": "..."}`.

Asks the payload to set the cancel flag on op N. The actual
cp_rf loop checks the flag every 4 MiB, so a multi-GiB copy
stops within ~one disk-IO worth of bytes (sub-second on PS5
NVMe). Returns `{"cancelled": true}` on success, `{"cancelled":
false}` if the op_id wasn't recognized (already finished or
never registered — both treated as success from the client's
perspective: "the op you wanted to cancel isn't running").

op_id.description:
Optional unique 64-bit identifier the client generates so it
can poll progress (`/api/ps5/fs/op-status`) and cancel
(`/api/ps5/fs/op-cancel`) the in-flight delete. Only used by
`ps5_fs_delete`; other handlers that share this struct (e.g.
`ps5_fs_mkdir`) ignore it. Pass 0 (or omit) for ops where
progress/cancel isn't needed; the payload skips its
in-flight-ops slot registration in that case so single-file
unlinks don't burn one of MAX_FS_OPS=4 slots.

offset.description:
Where to start reading (default 0). A bug report reads the TAIL of a log that has
outgrown the 256 KiB preview cap: the newest lines are the ones that explain a crash.

bytes_b64.description:
Base64 of the file contents. Base64 because this is a JSON body and the
payload's FS_WRITE_BYTES frame takes base64 anyway.

create_only.description: Refuse if the path already exists. Default false (overwrite).

Game.description: One game: everything in the collection with its Game ID.

cover_stamp.description:
The saved cover file's size and modified time, so a cover read out again (a deep
rescan) gets a new URL and the UI does not keep showing the old one.

local_cover.description: The cover file in the covers folder, when one was read out of the game.

title_source.description:
Where the title came from: `package` (the game itself), `dlc`, `online`, or empty (the
Game ID).

params.description: The full PARAM (SFO or param.json), in source order.

partial.description: Only header facts: PARAM was missing or encrypted.

has_icon.description: True iff `sce_sys/icon0.png` exists and is non-empty on the PS5. The UI uses this to decide whether to render an pointing at /api/ps5/game-icon — skipping the request for folders without an icon avoids a pointless 404 round-trip.

items.description: Files, or saves for the saves group.

HealOutcome.description: Result row per file we considered.

copied.description:
Pre-computed counts so the renderer doesn't have to filter the
outcomes vec.

outcomes.description:
Per-file outcomes in HEAL_FILES order. UI renders them as a
table so the user can see exactly what changed.

detail.description: What we actually observed, with numbers where we have them.

detail_id.description:
Which sentence `detail` is, with its values, for a client to say it in its own language
(`title` goes by `id`). `detail` and `remedy` stay plain English for everything else.

fix.description: Present only when the engine can actually perform the repair.

remedy.description: What the user should do. Empty when the check passed.

paths.description:
For `clean_junk`: the files the user was shown. Anything else is left alone, and so is one
of these no longer on the list. Absent: everything on the list at this moment.

error.description: Why it failed (`err` from icon_set, `error` from hidden_list).

hidden.description: Title ids whose home-screen icon is hidden in any user's icon table.

report_hex.description:
One 16-byte report as 32 hex characters: buttons, modifiers, dx (i16 LE), dy (i16 LE),
wheel, hwheel, then up to 8 HID usage IDs held.

Hub.description: Written by hand in the engine: the source has no field list for this.

HwInfo.description: Static hardware info. `physmem` is in bytes.

kernel_fw_version.description:
Sony's packed firmware version word, read from kernel data
memory via the SDK's `kernel_get_fw_version()` helper. 0 when
kernel R/W is unavailable on the running payload (no kstuff
loaded, or payload doesn't have the required perms) — in that
case fall back to the kern.version string parse on the
desktop side. Precise enough to distinguish FW points within
a family (e.g. 9.60 vs 9.6010).

boot_time_sec.description:
When the console booted, in seconds since the epoch on the console's own clock (to
compare with file times there); 0 from a helper that doesn't say.

load_avg_1m.description:
System load average (1, 5, 15 minute windows) via the SDK's
`getloadavg()` — added to prospero-libc in the 2026-05
ps5-payload-dev/sdk update. Stored as fractional values
(e.g. 0.42 = 42% of one core average); the payload sends
integer centi-units on the wire and the engine divides by
100 here so consumers get a normal `f32`. Negative value
means the getloadavg call failed on this firmware (the
payload encodes that as -1.00).

HwStorage.description:
"Console Storage" aggregate that matches what PS5 Settings shows.
Sums the three partitions Sony's UI counts (`/user effective +
/system_data + /system_ex`) and accounts for the reserved-pool slice
the FS keeps for root. Per-partition fields are also surfaced for
the diagnostics card. Distinct from `fs_list_volumes`: that returns
per-volume detail; this is the single-line summary.

HwTemps.description:
Live sensor readings. Values of 0 mean "API not available on this
firmware" rather than "actually zero" -- there's no thermal state
where any of these are legitimately 0 during normal operation.

cpu_core_measured_mhz.description:
The clock each of the eight cores really ran at while busy, in MHz, measured with a
timed chain of adds; indexed like `cpu_core_mhz`. `0` = not measured (the game cores
are not open to the helper) or outside 400–5000 MHz.

cpu_core_mhz.description:
The eight CPU cores' clocks in MHz: the power controller's figure for each core's
P-state, not a cycle count. `0` = unknown or outside 400–4000 MHz. Empty when the clocks
were not read.

cpu_core_mhz_min.description: Lowest and highest of the known `cpu_core_mhz` values; `0` when none is known.

cpu_freq_mhz.description:
A fixed REFERENCE clock (`sceKernelGetCpuFrequency`, 800 MHz on every console measured),
not what the cores run at; see `cpu_core_mhz` for those.

cpu_measure_src.description:
How the measured clocks came: `"add_chain"` (timed on the console, this read or an
earlier one), `"unsupported"` (no CPU took the measuring thread and nothing was measured
earlier; the next read tries again), or `""` (not asked for, or an older helper).

cpu_temp_rc.description:
How the last read of the CPU temperature went: Sony's return code (`"0x00000000"` is
success), `"fault"` (the call crashed and was recovered), `"missing"` (no such call on
this firmware), `"range"` (it answered with an impossible value) or `"none"` (no read has
finished yet). `None` from an older helper. Says why `cpu_temp` is 0.

cpu_usage_pct.description:
Average CPU usage across cores, 0–100 %. `-1` = unavailable (the
API isn't exported on this firmware, or an older payload that
doesn't send the field). Read on demand only.

extended_error.description:
Set when only the basic temperatures could be read: why the full read failed. Everything
beyond the temperatures then reads as unavailable.

fan_duty_pct.description:
Current fan duty, 0–100 % (approximate — the raw scale is
firmware-dependent). `-1` = unavailable. Read on demand only.

fan_filtered_c.description:
The fan controller's own filtered temperature (°C, one decimal). `None` when unreadable,
out of 20–110 °C, or from an older helper.

fan_guard.description:
The guard that keeps the pinned target: `"off"` (nothing pinned), `"ok"`, or
`"failing"` (its writes kept failing, so it stopped and the console's own control is in
charge until the next set). Empty from an older helper.

fan_last_restore_s.description: Seconds since the last of those restores; `-1` = never (or an older helper).

fan_pinned_c.description:
User-pinned fan threshold (°C). `0` = no custom threshold set
(fan runs at firmware default). A positive value means the user
has set a permanent fan speed that the helper puts back within
about 2 s whenever the system resets it (a game starting or closing).
Always available (even on basic read) since it's an in-process
value, not a sensor syscall.

fan_restores.description:
How many times this helper session put the pinned target back after the system reset
it. `0` also for an older helper.

fan_stock_c.description:
The console's own value: what the controller held before ps5upload first changed
it (°C). `0` = never seen. 91 on FW 13.60, not the 60 this app long assumed.

fan_target_c.description:
The temperature the fan controller is working to right now, read back from the
console (°C). `-1` = not reported (an older helper) or unreadable.

gpu_clock_src.description:
Where the clocks came from: `"mp1"` (read; while the driver is busy, the last values or
zeros), `"unsupported"` (the driver refused; the helper does not try again until it
restarts), or `""` (not asked for, or an older helper).

m2_temp.description:
M.2 NVMe expansion slot temperature (°C). Channel 2 of the SoC
sensor array. `0` = no M.2 drive installed or sensor unavailable.
Requires >= 20 to be treated as valid (empty slot returns 0).

measure_busy.description:
The measuring read has not come back, so `cpu_measure_src` and the measured clocks say
nothing. `false` from an older helper.

mp1_busy.description:
The power controller's read has not come back (seen for as long as a game runs), so
`gpu_clock_src` and the core clocks say nothing. `false` from an older helper.

product_shape.description:
Raw Sony "basic product shape" code (distinguishes hardware
families). `-1` = unavailable. The desktop maps known codes to a
label and otherwise shows the number; the model string remains the
primary identifier. Read on demand only.

read_ms.description:
How long the last read of the basic sensors took, in ms; with `stale`, how long the read
still running has taken so far. `None` from an older helper.

soc_clock_mhz.description:
The GPU (GFX) clock in MHz from the SoC's power controller (`/dev/mp1`), read only when
the clocks were asked for (`hw_temps_with_clocks`). `0` = not read, unsupported, or
outside 100–2500 MHz.

soc_temp_rc.description: The same for the SoC temperature.

stale.description:
Another request's read was still running, so these are the last values it had (0 if it
had none): the helper answers at once rather than queueing behind a stalled sensor call.

exe_platform.description:
`ps4` or `ps5` as `eboot.bin`'s process param says (its SDK words), when it has one
that can be read. `platform` falls back to it when the title id says nothing.

titles.description: Title per language (param.json locale, or the SFO `TITLE_xx` code).

ImageDestinationReq.description: Where an image build puts the image.

oneOf.description:
A PS5: `addr` (its address) and `dir` (an absolute folder on it, made when missing). A
dropped connection goes on where it stopped, and so does the same build started again.

A saved server (`source_id`, a connection under Connections: SMB, NFS, FTP, SFTP or
WebDAV) and `dir`, a folder on it (made when missing). Written there as `<name>.partial`,
read back there and only then renamed, never over anything; the job's `dest` is then
`remote://<source_id>/<dir>/<name>`. On SMB, NFS and SFTP a write that was cut off goes
on from what the server holds.

ImageEditReq.description:
One change for an edited copy of an image: `{"op":"delete","path":…}` removes a file or
folder; `{"op":"put","path":…,"from":…}` puts a file (or a folder's contents) from this
computer at `path`, replacing what is there.

ImageKind.description: A game image file system, as ShadowMount+ names it by extension.

via_api.description:
Opened through ShadowMount+'s API (`games/mount` read-write) rather than a `config.ini`
rule; closed the same way. Absent in a journal from before 9.4.0.

save_path.description: The PS4 save folder of the game on the PS5 (from the saves list, kind "ps4").

src_dir.description: The local folder with the PS4's files of that game.

left.description: Left stick [x, y], each -1..1 (right and down positive).

InspectResponse.description:
What `/api/fpkg/inspect` answers: the inspection, plus the lowest firmware the game can
run on when its modules say so (see `fpkg_firmware`).

Inspection.description:
What a caller learns before deciding to build: what the source is, whether it looks
like a launchable title, what the package will cost, and whether there is room.

ampr_packs.description:
For a libSceAmpr title, whether an image can carry LZ4 asset packs (see
[`crate::ampr_pack::image::readiness`]); `None` for any other title.

checks.description: Every readiness finding, passes and warnings alike.

content_version.description: The version it says it is: `contentVersion`, or a PS4 game's `APP_VER`.

output_free.description: Bytes free where the output would go; `None` where the platform does not say.

planned_size.description: The package's estimated size (what the free-space check uses).

ps4_addon_data.description: An add-on: whether it holds files (`false`: a licence, nothing to convert).

ps4_game.description: A PS4 game, update or add-on: it becomes an image or a folder, not a PS5 package.

ps4_kind.description:
What a PS4 source is: `game`, `patch` (an update, which goes into its game: see
[`crate::ps4_merge`]) or `addon`. Absent for a PS5 one.

ps4_merge.description: Inspected with an update merged in: what the merge is.

ps4_title_id.description: The PS4 title it is or belongs to (`CUSA…`): an update's or add-on's game.

unsigned_executables.description: How many of its executables are plain ELF files, which a build fake-signs.

force_stream.description:
Skip the console-local attempt and serve the package from this engine through
the installer daemon ("Retry with Stream" after 0x80B2116F). Only meaningful for a
`console_path` source; see [`stream_retry_allowed`].

insecure_tls.description:
Skip certificate checks when THIS engine fetches a link. Never applies to the
console's own fetch.

proxy_link.description:
For a link: this engine downloads it and serves it to the console ("Stream through
this computer"), instead of handing the console the link to fetch by itself. Without
it the console is given the link first, and a link only this computer can reach (a
private server, a VPN, localhost) simply failed with a network error.

InstallPreflightResponse.description:
What the console already has, for the package the user is about to install.

The engine's own artifact matching is the answer to "is this installed?"
deliberately lives HERE rather than in the client: the client used to compare
fingerprints itself and disagreed with the engine, so a PS5 FPKG could be
reported as not-installed in the UI while the engine's own completion check
considered it installed (Sony writes a debug package's *inner* image as
`app.pkg`, so its size and hash can never equal the outer container's).

category.description: `category` from the package being asked about (`gd`, `gp`, `ac`).

detail.description: Human-readable one-liner for the UI; empty when nothing needs saying.

installed_artifacts.description: The console's artifacts for this title, so the UI can show what IS there.

installed_version.description: The version currently installed, when the console reports one.

state.description:
`installed`                 — these exact bytes are already on the console
`different_version_installed` — the title has this kind of artifact, but not this build
`base_missing`              — a patch/add-on with no base game to apply to
`not_installed`             — nothing for this title in this category
`unknown`                   — the console couldn't be read; never act on this

may_not_launch.description:
Always false for a serve-only start; the launch caution now comes
from the unified install status's `may_not_launch` verdict.

package_type.description:
The package_type the install actually ran with, AFTER the engine's
staged-pkg category parse (so a "…DP" here means "this was treated as a
patch"). Lets the client recognise guarded patch/DLC hand-offs even on
USB/queue/File-System paths where it sent no type, then select the safe
category-aware DPI fallback.

register_path.description:
2.2.52 diagnostics — surfaced to the UI's "Advanced details"
expander for failed installs. Empty / false on older payloads.
`register_path` reports which BGFT Register variant ran
("intdebug" / "regular" / "none"); `intdebug_avail` is whether
the IntDebug symbol resolved at all (false = fakepkg installs
effectively unsupported on this firmware regardless of cred);
`kernel_rw` mirrors the payload's process-wide cred-elevation
state.

shellui_err.description:
Legacy per-tier err codes from the retired in-process cascade. The
serve-only start never sets them; kept for response-shape stability.

via.description:
Always "serve-only": the unified orchestrator hands the session URL
to the installer daemon.

image_backed.description:
Only meaningful for origin=="registered": backed by a mounted
disk image (.exfat/.ffpkg) vs a plain folder registration.

source.description:
Only meaningful for origin=="registered": the source path we
registered the title from (empty otherwise).

system.description:
True for NPXS-prefixed system apps — the UI greys these and
requires a stronger confirm before uninstalling.

incomplete.description:
True when the list may be missing titles: a directory listing hit its page size,
or app.db could not be read in full (a failed query, or a helper that could not
deliver every row, #473). The titles shown are real; there may be more.

registered_unavailable.description:
True if app_list_registered() failed (e.g. older payload) — the
UI then can't reliably tag the "registered" group, so it shows
everything under "installed" with a soft note rather than erroring.

source.description:
Where this list comes from: read from the console now (`/api/games/installed` is what
saved consoles had when last read; `/api/pkg/installed` is one title's package files).

InstalledGame.description: One title installed on some saved console, for the command palette.

hosts.description: The consoles (bare IPs) it was last read as installed on.

title.description: The console's name for it, else the Collection's; "" when neither knows one.

content_id.description:
Best-effort header ContentID. Useful for legacy staged rows whose
fingerprint was not cached.

fingerprint.description: Same bounded sampled-BLAKE3 identity emitted by the local parser.

new.description: A new room and key: the old internet link stops working.

internet.description: Also an internet invite: a room on the signalling hub (`invite.internet.url`).

new.description: A new key (the old link stops working).

share.description:
The one link, as "Invites work" says: the internet invite when that is "anywhere" (and the
hub address and certificate allow it), else the home network's; never refused for it.

JobStage.description: Where a staged job stands: the stage's id and place in the sequence, and its own bytes.

bytes_finalized.description:
Cumulative bytes the payload has finalized so far during
apply. Lets the UI show a second progress dimension
(bytes-finalized / total-bytes) for cases where file
sizes vary wildly. 0 outside the finalize phase.

bytes_sent.description:
Bytes sent so far. Updated on a timer (200 ms) that reads the
shared AtomicU64 the shard loop increments in
`ps5upload_core::TransferConfig::progress_bytes`. Lets the UI
render a real progress bar + speed + ETA during a running
transfer, instead of guessing from elapsed time alone.

files_count.description:
Ordered list of files this job will send. For folder uploads
this is the planned delta (reconcile) or the full tree walk
(plain dir); for single files / file-list uploads, the
requested file(s). The job snapshot (poll, list, events) carries
only its length as `files_count`: a big folder's list is
megabytes and was re-sent on every 500 ms poll. The list itself
is served once by `GET /api/jobs/{id}/files`.

files_finalized.description:
P3 / v2.18.0 — files the PS5 has fully written to their
destination paths during the post-100% COMMIT_TX apply
loop. Only ticks once `bytes_sent == total_bytes`; until
then this stays at 0. The payload emits APPLY_PROGRESS
frames every ~1 sec or 1024 files during apply when the
engine sent `TX_FLAG_APPLY_PROGRESS_REQUESTED` on
BEGIN_TX (default for multi-file uploads). UI surfaces
this as "Finalized N of M files" during the finalize
phase so users see real motion through what used to be
a silent 10-30 min wait.

0 for single-file uploads (apply is one fsync, no
progress reporting), for old payloads that don't emit
APPLY_PROGRESS (graceful degradation — UI shows the
plain "Finalizing on PS5…" pill from v2.17.3), and
during the pre-finalize bytes-on-wire phase.

files_finalizing_total.description:
Total files the payload will commit. Same value as
`files.len()` on the planned manifest, surfaced here as
a u64 so the UI doesn't have to count `files`. 0 means
"unknown" — single-file uploads or pre-FIRST-frame
(we set this on the first APPLY_PROGRESS arrival).

files_processing.description:
Per-file progress — climbs as each source file is read into a
pack frame or as its first chunk goes out. The shard-ACK-based
`bytes_sent` looks like "start → finished" on 46 k-file game
folders (each packed ACK completes ~200 files at once); this
counter ticks smoothly through the read-many-tiny-files phase
so the user sees the upload is alive. 0 means "not provided
by this transfer path" (e.g. single-file uploads), in which
case the UI falls back to its size-derived estimate.

skipped_bytes.description: Bytes those skipped files represent. 0 for non-reconcile.

skipped_files.description:
Files already present on the PS5 that were skipped this run
(reconcile mode only). 0 for non-reconcile uploads.

stage.description: The stage a staged job (an FPKG build) is in; `None` for jobs without stages.

total_bytes.description:
Total bytes expected for this job (source size). 0 if
unknown at job start (should only happen for transfers that
fail to stat the source, which would error before Running).

commit_ack.description:
Full COMMIT_TX_ACK body as a parsed JSON value — surfaces PS5-side
timing (timing_us) and pool counters (pack_records etc.) in the
engine job record so bench sweeps can persist them without an
extra round-trip.

files_sent.description:
File count + skipped count for the summary card. `files_sent`
excludes skipped files; `skipped_files` counts what reconcile
mode found already-present on the PS5.

error.description:
Raw stringified error chain. Kept for debuggability and as
the fallback rendering when structured fields below are
absent (older payloads, non-payload-origin errors).

error_console.description:
The console the failure came from, when it names one (a PS5-to-PS5 relay talks
to two). The client opens the pairing dialog for THIS console, not the one it
happens to be watching the job against.

error_detail.description:
Human-readable detail from the payload's error frame
`"detail"` field. Often pinpoints the on-PS5 path or the
underlying errno. Shown to the user as the secondary line
in the error card.

error_reason.description:
Machine-parseable error category lifted from the payload's
error frame body (`{"error":"direct_writer_io_error",…}`).
`None` for errors that didn't originate from the payload's
JSON-bodied error frames — e.g. local I/O, connection
refused at TCP-connect time. UI uses this to humanize the
surface text.

error_space.description:
The figures behind a refusal for lack of room, which the client words in the user's
language (`error` and `error_detail` hold the English, for logs and scripts).

password.description: The drive's password, when it has one.

KeyboardReq.description: No Debug: what is typed may be private.

text.description: The whole text of the console's field.

categories.description:
Per-category levels; a category set to null loses its override. Replaces the overrides
when given (with `merge: true`, only the named categories change).

level.description: The global level: error, warn, info, debug or trace.

merge.description: Change only the categories named, keeping the other overrides.

minutes.description: How long a raise lasts from now, in minutes (instead of `until_ms`): at most 1440, a day.

reset.description: Start from the default (info, no overrides) before the rest.

until_ms.description: When a raise ends, Unix ms.

Link.description: One side's link, as far as it could be read.

detail.description: Extra words for the skip (an error text), never shown as a verdict.

link_mbps.description: The negotiated speed of a wired link in Mb/s, when the system reports it.

skip.description:
Why the link could not be read; `None` when it was. A short code the client words:
`mobile`, `container`, `no_route`, `unreadable`, `not_found`, `helper`.

filename.description:
The name the file should have: Content-Disposition, else the last segment of the
FINAL url (after redirects). Never empty for a non-refused link.

image.description:
A game image ShadowMount+ mounts as it is (by its header, else its name): `exfat`,
`ufs`, `pfs`. Only for `File`; an `.lz4`'s image is in `lz4`.

lz4.description:
A `.lz4` stream (any name): what it unpacks to on the way to the console. Only for
`File`, filled in by [`probe`] from the first decoded block.

message.description: A sentence for the user. Only for `Refused`.

ranges.description: The origin answered the ranged request with 206, so the parallel fetcher can read it.

ps5_addr.description: The console the link is for: picks the address of this computer it can reach.

LinkDownloadReq.description: `/api/link/download` request: download a link's file to a console folder.

dest_dir.description: Absolute console folder the file lands in.

file_name.description: Overrides the name the link supplies.

unpack.description: An `.lz4` link is unpacked on the way (the default); false keeps the `.lz4` as it is.

any.description: True: any device on the network may fetch it. False: only the console it was made for.

hub.description: The drive's home there: a folder, or (with `hub_name`) where a new one is made.

name.description: What the two consoles are called (shown on each side's card).

Live.description: Written by hand in the engine: the source has no field list for this.

LocalInventoryEntry.description: A file in the local cache.

mtime.description: File mtime, seconds since the Unix epoch.

path.description: Path of the cached `.elf`: what a send consumes.

version.description: Tag of the cached binary, from the `VERSION` file beside it.

Location.description: One place a game is: a package, an image, a folder, an archive.

added_ts.description: Unix seconds of `added_at`, for sorting (strings from other tools may differ in form).

container.description: The top folder under the root, for display only (nothing keys on it).

date_source.description: `created` (file birth time) or `modified` (birth time not available).

parts.description:
The location's other files, when it is more than one: the later parts of a split package
or the later volumes of a `.rar` set (`absolute_path` is the first). They count in
`size_bytes` and go wherever it goes.

root.description: The library root this location is under.

owner.description: The window asking (a browser of this engine): its locks are its own.

Lz4Info.description: What a `.lz4` link unpacks to, as the probe reports it.

image.description: The game image inside, when it is one ShadowMount+ mounts.

unpacked_name.description:
The name it gets on the console: the link's name without `.lz4`, with the image's
extension when the name has none ShadowMount+ knows.

unpacked_size.description:
The unpacked size, when the stream or the image header states it. `None` means the
link cannot be streamed to the console (see `unsupported`).

unsupported.description: Why it cannot be streamed, in a sentence for the user.

available.description: This engine runs on a Mac, so these can be read and changed.

finder_network_off.description: Finder writes no `.DS_Store` on network shares / USB drives.

MergeInfo.description: What a merge is: for the screen and the log.

replaced.description: Files of the game the update replaces, and files it adds.

MicReq.description: A local script's mic: on or off, and Opus packets while no page is attached.

base.description:
Base address as a hex string ("0x7f1234..."). String form
because JSON numbers can't represent u64 across all renderers
(JS Number is f64, can lose precision past 2^53).

count.description:
How many modules the console listed. `refused` of them have no row: Sony would not
describe them, and `refused_rc` is what it said. An older helper sends none of these.

f_bsize.description:
statfs-reported block size at the resolved mount point. Added
in 2.2.52 to help diagnose UFS images that mount at the kernel
level but read as empty (typically a sector-size/cluster-size
mismatch between the image and the LVD-exposed device). Older
payloads omit the field; serde-default to 0 so a missing value
doesn't read as a fake validation failure on pre-2.2.52 mounts.

f_iosize.description:
statfs-reported preferred I/O block size. Same diagnostics
purpose as `f_bsize` — useful when the kernel reports a
fragment size for `f_bsize` and the actual I/O block size lives
here instead. Added in 2.2.52.

kernel_ro.description:
True if the kernel reports `MNT_RDONLY` on the resolved mount
point — even when the caller passed `read_only=false`. PS5's
UFS_DOWNLOAD_DATA image_type forces RO on some firmwares and
surfacing this lets the UI explain to the user why writes
won't land. Added in 2.2.52.

layout_valid.description:
True if `<mount_point>/sce_sys/param.json` exists immediately
after the mount. False when the user built an image with an
extra top-level folder (game files at
`<mount>/MyGame/sce_sys/...` instead of `<mount>/sce_sys/...`)
or when the image isn't a game (e.g. an arbitrary disk image).
The mount itself succeeds either way; this flag lets the UI
warn that Register/Launch will fail without re-building the
image. Added in 2.2.32. Older payloads omit the field — serde
defaults to `true` so a missing field doesn't trigger a false
warning on pre-2.2.32 payloads.

container.description: The collection folder this move is inside (absolute).

set.description:
A part of a split package: its set, named by the set's first file as it is now. A set
moves as one: all of it, or none of it.

position.description: Among the console's waiting items, from 0. Past the end means the end.

flags.description:
Raw flags from sceNetGetIfList. Bit set carries link state +
other Sony-internal flags.

NotifClearResult.description: Result of clearing the notification ring.

NpState.description:
What the console says about a user's PlayStation Network sign-in state: whether a backup
from before np-fake-signin ran is kept on it, and the values that decide how the console
treats the account (np-fake-signin writes NP_sub_account 2, NP_offl_acct_adult 0 and an age
from its template). `None` where the registry could not be read.

backup.description: A backup from before the first sign-in is on the console.

Observation.description:
One sighting of this exact library set: which game shipped it, on which
console, and what that game is.

Sets are content-addressed, so two consoles carrying the same backported
game collapse into ONE entry — and the second sighting used to be thrown
away with the duplicate. Keeping every sighting is what lets the ranking
prefer a combination that two different consoles both actually run over one
seen a single time.

console_key.description:
Stable identity of the console it was seen on.

`console` is a DISPLAY name and is not stable: the same machine was
recorded as `phat-5.10` by one scan and `192.0.2.99` by the next,
which made `same_source` treat one console as two and inflate a set's
own evidence. The host does not change when the user renames a roster
entry, so the dedupe keys on this when both sides have it.

image_backed.description:
Disk-image (ShadowMount) title rather than a plain folder. Recorded
because it changes how the title is edited, not because it ranks.

Offer.description: A package in the collection the console could take.

category.description: `gd`, `gp` or `ac`, which orders installs base → update → DLC.

image.description: The real image under /user/home ("" when nothing is open).

OpenSettingsRequest.description:
Observe how many bytes the install has consumed so far, from the two
physical signals. Returns the larger of (free-space drop on the data
volume since the baseline) and (sum of the title dir's file sizes). Both
are best-effort: an unreadable signal contributes 0, not an error — the
tracker degrades to whichever signal is available.

moves.description: The moves the user kept ticked in the preview.

console_key.description:
Stable identity of the console — its host — as opposed to the
display name above, which the user can rename at will.

title_name.description:
The game's name, for showing where a set came from without a
second lookup. Defaults so corpora written before it survive.

oneOf.description: Harvested from a game on a console.
Uploaded by the user as one pack.

PairResult.description: What a successful pairing leaves us with.

account_id_b64.description:
Which account the console paired with, and how it was chosen —
passed through from readiness so the UI can name it.

credential.description: The number a WAKEUP carries. This is the whole point.

regist_key.description:
Session credentials returned by the same registration handshake.
Keeping these in the result lets the client configure Wake & sign in
without asking the user to copy secrets out of Chiaki manually.

Both are the 16-byte form as 32 hex characters — what
[`crate::rp_session::SessionCreds::from_hex`] parses and what the UI
stores. The console reports the regist key as the ASCII text alone
(16 hex chars), so it is NUL-padded here: an unpadded value fails the
client's 32-hex check and the sign-in keys are silently dropped.

user_name.description:
The paired user's name on the console, when it could be read (the helper's user list), for
telling a console's paired users apart. Empty when not known.

code.description: The six digits typed from the console's screen: a string (leading zeros) or a number.

current.description: The current one, for a device that is not in the drive.

password.description: The new password; empty or absent removes it.

PathStat.description: What `fs.stat` says about a path (a symbolic link is followed; a dangling one is `link`).

dev.description: The device id (`st_dev`): two paths with the same value share a mount.

PayloadRestoreRequest.description:
`POST /api/pkg/payload-restore` — (re)send the bundled MAIN ps5upload
payload to the console's loader (:9021). The desktop app does this itself
(it holds the ELF and can open the socket); the self-hosted web UI cannot,
so it asks the engine — which is what `ensurePayloadCurrent` /
`restoreMainPayload` call in the browser build to redeploy a stale or dead
helper. Install-time restore is handled inside the unified install state
machine; this route is for the general payload-freshness path only.

Never an HTTP error on a failed send: the browser caller runs it
best-effort and a failed restore is information to log, not a reason to
surface a red error over whatever prompted the refresh.

port.description: The USB port, beep pattern or brightness level the action takes; 0 otherwise.

PkgAuthenticity.description:
What the unencrypted package envelope can prove about signing. PS4 CNT
packages need a deeper cryptographic probe, so they intentionally remain
unknown instead of being mislabeled "retail" merely from `\x7FCNT`.

PkgInfo.description: What a package (or image, or folder) says about itself. Field names are the source app's.

error.description: Why it could not be read, when it could not.

min_fw.description:
The firmware the item asks for (`7.00`), from its param.json or PARAM.SFO. A PS4 item
names a PS4 firmware, which says nothing about a PS5's.

oneOf.description:
A `\x7FCNT` metadata container. This describes the container layout,
not whether its cryptographic material is retail or fake/debug.
A complete PS5 finalized image (`\x7FFIH`) with an embedded CNT.

Magic byte sequence we don't recognise. It may be a license-only
artifact, an unsupported package variant, or simply the wrong file.
The install UI may still permit an attempt; Sony's installer remains
the final authority on formats it accepts.

app_ver.description:
PARAM.SFO `APP_VER` field — the application version this package
brings, e.g. `01.04`. For a patch (`gp`) this is the authoritative
"which update is this" answer (a patch shares the base game's
content_id and TITLE, so nothing else distinguishes versions). Empty
when the SFO is missing or has no APP_VER key.

authenticity.description: Signing class proven by the package envelope.

content_flags.description: The container header's `content_flags` (0x78); the patch bits are 0x40100000.

content_id.description:
36-char content id (e.g. `EP0006-CUSA45456_00-...`). Empty for
`Unknown` kind. Trailing NULs trimmed.

content_type.description:
The container header's `content_type` (0x74): 0x1A/0x20 an application, 0x1B/0x21
additional content (DLC), 0x26 a PS5 system application. 0 when not read.

fingerprint.description:
Stable, inexpensive identity for this exact package variant. This is a
BLAKE3 digest over the file size plus bounded samples from the beginning
and end of the pkg. It deliberately differs for two patches that share
the same ContentID/category/APP_VER (for example an optional fix and a
backport), without making the UI hash a multi-gigabyte pkg before an
upload can start.

icon_png_base64.description: PNG bytes from ICON0.PNG entry, if present. None if the entry is missing or oversize. Base64-encoded for transport across the Tauri/HTTP boundary; the React side decodes for .

package_type.description: Mapping of category/platform to BGFT's package_type string.

path.description: Path of the PKG that was parsed. Single file, not the split set.

platform.description:
Target platform for UI badging: `"ps4"`, `"ps5"`, or `""` (unknown).
Derived from the header magic (`\x7FFIH` = PS5) and the title-id
prefix (CUSA = PS4, PPSA = PS5). See [`derive_platform`].

size.description:
Total bytes of the file on disk (sum across split parts when
present — see [`SplitPkgMetadata`]).

title.description: Title from PARAM.SFO key `TITLE`. Empty if SFO missing.

title_id.description:
Title id from PARAM.SFO key `TITLE_ID`. Often duplicated within
`content_id`; we surface both because some non-standard PKGs
have one without the other.

warnings.description:
Non-fatal warnings raised during parse — surfaced in the UI as
a yellow caution row. Empty for a clean stock PKG.

labels.description: How to show each container: its path, or "Server: /path" on a saved server.

PlanStatus.description:
The plan being made, or the last one: `POST .../plan/start` starts it (or joins it),
`GET .../plan/status` follows it, `POST .../plan/cancel` stops it.

done.description: Items looked at, of how many found so far.

phase.description:
`finding` (walking the folders) or `reading` (reading the packages the index does not
know), while running.

account_id.description: The PSN account id (base64 of its 8 bytes) to pair, with `pin`.

addr.description:
The payload's management address. Optional — falls back to the
engine's configured console, like every other payload call.

host.description:
The console's address. Registration and wake use their own ports,
so this is the bare host, not the management address.

pin.description:
The 8-digit PIN the PS5 shows under Settings › System › Remote Play › Link Device. With
it the engine registers on its own (no helper, any firmware); never logged.

user_name.description:
The paired user's name, for telling a console's paired users apart. Left out, the helper's
name for the user is used when it can be read. Pairing another user adds to the console's
paired users; pairing one again replaces that user's keys.

PowerTelemetry.description:
Power telemetry parsed from PowerTelemetry ACK body.

Each field is `Some` when ICC reported success, `None` when the
payload's ICC call returned an error and emitted `<key>=err`. The
renderer treats `None` as "this PS5 generation doesn't expose this
metric" rather than as a hard failure.

operating_seconds.description: Cumulative power-on seconds since first boot.

power_up_cause.description:
Reason for the most recent power-up (button, RTC, network).
Sony doesn't document the exact codes; surfaced raw.

status.description:
Why the fields above may be empty:
  `ok`                     all four values read
  `partial`                some read, some failed (FW 5.10)
  `calls_failed`           symbols exist but every call errored
  `unsupported_firmware`   no `sceKernelIccGet*` symbol resolves
                           (retail 9.60, verified on hardware)

Without this the client can only render four bare nulls as "—",
which reads like a bug rather than a firmware limitation. Older
payloads don't send it; `None` then means "unknown".

symbols_resolved.description: How many of the four ICC symbols exist on this firmware (0-4).

thermal_alert_flags.description: Bit-flagged thermal alert state. 0 = no alert.

values_ok.description:
How many actually returned a value (0-4). Deliberately separate
from `symbols_resolved`: FW 5.10 resolves all four but only two
succeed, so the symbol count alone would overstate support.

PowerWakeLoginReq.description:
POST /api/ps5/power/wake — wake a console in standby over Sony's DDP.

Not Wake-on-LAN: a PS5 does not wake from a magic packet (measured — nine
datagrams across every plausible port and address did nothing to a sleeping
console). This speaks the protocol the Remote Play app uses.

Fire-and-forget: the console never acknowledges a WAKEUP, so a 200 here
means the datagram was sent and nothing more. It also requires "Enable
Remote Play" on the console; with that off nothing is listening at all.

ask_passcode.description:
Someone is there to type the user's login passcode if the console asks: the sign-in is
held and the passcode asked for (wake_login_api). Otherwise (an automatic wake) a
passcode request ends it with the console awake at its sign-in screen.

regist_key.description:
Both hex, harvested from a pairing. Signing in needs the full session keys, not just the
wake credential; left out, the ones the engine keeps for this console are used.

user.description:
Which of the console's paired PS5 users to sign in (an account id, a name as
`GET /api/consoles` lists it under `rp_users`, or its number there), when the keys are left
out. Left out, the chosen user (the one Play starts as).

PowerWakeReq.description:
GET /api/ps5/power/telemetry — lifetime ICC telemetry (operating
seconds, boot cycles, thermal alerts, power-up cause).

credential.description:
`user-credential` captured from the PS Remote Play app. Without it the
console silently ignores the request.

host.description: The console's address. DDP is spoken to the console directly.

file.description: The file inside the copy, or empty for the copy as a whole.

ProcEntry.description:
One running process on the PS5. Kept minimal — PID and command name
is all the payload can surface cheaply from the allproc walk. Fields
are `String` rather than `&str` since this crosses the HTTP boundary
and needs to own its data.

error.description:
Optional short error code when `ok == false`. UI can map this
to a human string; raw codes match the `err_out` values in
`payload/src/proc_list.c`.

ok.description:
`false` when the payload can tell the walk didn't succeed
(typically `kernel_rw_unavailable`). `procs` may still be
partially populated if the failure happened mid-walk.

truncated.description:
Payload-reported truncation signal. `true` if the walk was cut
short (cap hit or a follow-pointer failure).

ProcessInfo.description:
One process row. Every field defaults so the payload's trailing
`{"truncated":true}` sentinel object (which carries no pid) parses
cleanly and is split off in `process_list`.

is_self.description:
True for the helper's OWN process. proc_kill refuses to kill it
(pid == getpid() → EPERM), so the UI disables Kill/Restart for it.

kind.description: "app" | "payload" | "system" — drives the UI's filter + kill guard.

name.description: Thread name (ki_tdname) — what the compact list has always shown.

title_id.description: Title id for app/game processes; empty for daemons/system.

truncated.description:
Set only on the synthetic last element when the payload truncated
the list to fit its buffer. Split out by `process_list`.

errno.description: Numeric errno from the failed kill (ESRCH/EPERM/…), 0 on success.

reason.description: Human-readable errno string (strerror) — e.g. "No such process".

truncated.description: True when the payload's buffer filled and the list was cut short.

id.description:
Accepts a JSON string ("0x1a2b" or decimal) as well as a number.

A number alone is not safe here: an account id is 64-bit, and a
JavaScript client cannot represent anything above 2^53 exactly — it
would round and silently activate a DIFFERENT id than the user typed.
The string form is what the client sends; the number form stays for
any older caller.

image_path.description:
Host-side path to the source image the user picked (same model as
the zip/7z handlers, which take a host `archive_path`).

ProfileInfo.description: Foreground user + local users + account-name slots, from PROFILE_INFO.

uid.description:
Foreground user id, or 0 when the payload daemon has no active
session (common — prefer `users` for a target).

users.description: Every local user on the console (the avatar can target any of them).

ProfileNpReq.description:
The PSN sign-in backup routes: the account slot np-fake-signin matches the user to, and the
user (0 or absent = the foreground user).

offline_activated.description:
Activated by OUR offline flow (flags == 0x1002) rather than by a
real PSN link. `activated` says it works; this says how it got there.

ProfileUsernameReq.description:
POST /api/transfer/7z — start a 7z-archive upload job. Same job/progress/SSE
plumbing and resume semantics as the zip path; the progress denominator is
the total uncompressed size.

Ps4Kind.description: What a PS4 package is: see the module docs.

adopt.description:
#444, a send another device started (its `tx_id`): `take` ends both consoles' halves and
sends again here, resuming from the receiving console's journal; `watch` follows a direct
send still running between the consoles and drives it from here on.
