bandwidth_cap_mbps.description: Paces the relay like an upload's cap (the environment's cap otherwise).

direct_addr.description:
What the sending console dials to reach the receiving one (`host[:port]`, IPv4), in
place of the receiving console's own address: a local forward on the sending console
(ps5-tailscale), or a NAT the consoles see differently from this computer.

RarInspectReq.description: `/api/rar/inspect` request. Desktop-only, same gate as the handler.

RarPackagesReq.description: `/api/rar/packages` request (every archive kind: the name predates ZIP and 7z).

Rates.description:
The measured speeds behind an estimate, bytes per second (`read`: the source; `write`: the
output drive; the rest: the encoder on every thread at each level).

ReaderMetadata.description:
The subset of [`PkgMetadata`] recoverable from ranged reads — enough to
enrich a listing row without parsing the whole file.

authenticity.description: Signing class proven by the outer envelope.

content_flags.description: The container header's `content_flags` (0x78); 0 when not read.

content_type.description: The container header's `content_type` (0x74); 0 when not read. See [`kind::classify`].

fingerprint.description:
Optional sampled artifact identity. `metadata_from_reader` leaves this
empty because it does not know the total file size; remote callers that
do know it can populate the field with
[`package_fingerprint_from_reader`].

Readiness.description: Whether a libSceAmpr title can be packed, as the Convert screen shows it.

emulator_missing.description:
The game reads through AMPR and ships no emulator at all: it may not start from an image
or folder without one, packs or not ([`emulator_needed_at`]).

kind.description:
`ok`; `runtime` (the game's ampr_emu is missing or too old: installing
[`RUNTIME_VERSION`] into the image makes packs possible); `no_ampr` (the game does not
read through AMPR, so nothing could serve packs: .ffpfsc is its compression).

refusal.description: Why packing is refused; `None` when it can go ahead.

runtime_version.description: The version the game's `ampr_emu` reports, when its module says.

RemotePlayReadiness.description:
Everything that decides whether Remote Play can work on this console.

The payload sends 0/1 integers for the flags rather than JSON booleans,
so these are `u8` and converted by the helpers below. Do not "simplify"
them to `bool` and expect serde to coerce — it will not, and the frame
will fail to parse. See the payload↔engine key contract note.

account_uid.description:
The user whose account pairing will actually use. Usually the
foreground one; falls back to the first signed-in activated user.

foreground_uid.description:
The user in the foreground, or -1 when there is none. Reported
literally — a console can sit signed in with nobody in front.

registry_err.description:
Non-zero means the registry could not be READ — which is very
different from "the setting is off". Everything else in this struct
is meaningless when it is set.

err.description:
Diagnostic the payload writes when entering a FAILED/TIMEOUT state
(e.g. "sceRemoteplayInitialize failed: 0x8094xxxx"). Surfaced to the
UI so the user sees *why* the PIN couldn't be generated, not just
the bare word "failed".

probes.description:
ConfirmDeviceRegist probes made for the live PIN, and the last answer (rc, status,
reason code). Diagnostics only: `state` is already the payload's verdict. Absent
(zero) from payloads before the pairing-state rewrite.

insecure_tls.description:
Skip the certificate check for this read, as the install it precedes will. A probe
that always verified made "Skip the certificate check" useless: the link was refused
here, before the install it was ticked for ever started.

keep_previous.description: Keep the copy being replaced as `<path>.prev` first.

local_path.description:
The helper ELF on this computer (the desktop app's bundled one); otherwise the
engine's own bundled image.

path.description: The stored copy on the console.

action.description:
keep_copy (it replaces the original), keep_original (the copy goes to the trash),
keep_both (the copy gets a name of its own).

copy.description: The conflict copy's path in the drive.

name.description: keep_both: the copy's new file name (default: "<name> (from <device>)").

save_path.description: The save folder on the console (from the saves list).

server.description: The backup is on the network share (#592), not in the backup folder.

Run.description: What a running Workshop job is making, for a client that did not start it.

source.description: What the user chose: the archive, for a game unpacked from one.

label.description: How to show the folder: its path, or "Server: /path" on a saved server.

unreadable.description:
Its log could not be read (cut short by a power cut, say): a run happened, and what it
moved cannot be undone from here.

RuntimeChoice.description: Which ampr-emu-ng goes into a packed game.

kind.description:
"ps5" for native, "ps4" for legacy savedata. Lets the UI
group by platform without re-parsing path strings.

truncated.description: True when the payload's list buffer filled and later saves were not listed.

image.description: The save image under /user/home; empty or absent only reports what is open.

path.description: The save folder on the console it came from.

console_key.description:
Stable identity of the console (its host). `console` is a display name
the user can change; keying the sighting dedupe on it made one machine
count as two.

titles.description:
Titles to walk. Supplied by the client, which already has them from
/api/ps5/apps/installed — enumerating them again here would duplicate a
large handler for no gain.

current.description: The folder being searched, or the item or game being read.

error.description: Why the last scan stopped, when it failed.

games.description: Games and locations the last good scan found.

phase.description:
While running: `finding` (walking the folders), `reading` (identifying each item),
`naming` (titles and covers), `saving`.

unreadable.description: Folders the last good scan could not read (what it found there before is kept).

image_backed.description:
Disk-image (ShadowMount) title. Recorded with the sighting because it
is free here — the client already has it — and it says how the source
game is stored without a second lookup.

truncated.description: True when the payload's list buffer filled and later files were not listed.

SdkOverlayStatus.description:
The payload's fakelib-overlay status, forwarded verbatim from the SdkScan
ack (`fakelib_overlay_status_json`).

This MUST be declared here even though nothing in the engine reads it: the
handler deserializes the payload's ack into `SdkScanResponse` and then
re-serializes it for the client, so any field missing from this struct is
silently dropped in transit. It was missing, so `overlay` never reached the
UI, `backportOverlayReady()` saw `undefined`, and the Backport button stayed
disabled behind "Library overlay is not available — send the current
payload" on consoles already running the current payload.

patch_libc.description: Opt-in libc.prx symbol swap — see sdk_changer.rs.

overlay.description:
Absent on payloads older than the overlay work; `None` then, which the
UI treats as "not available" — the same thing it showed before, but now
for the real reason rather than because the engine ate the field.

truncated.description:
The console has more titles than fit its reply and stopped listing at a
whole entry. Declared for the same reason as `overlay`: a field missing
here is dropped on the way to the client, and the list would look
complete. Absent (false) from helpers that predate it.

"Guests play as": the console profile a guest on Player `player` gets, chosen by the host for
one console (user ids are that console's). The helper seats the guest's pad in it as it is made
(`vpad.open` with `bind_user`), so the console never asks "Who's using this controller?" and the
guest cannot pick another profile. No entry for a player: the console asks (as before).

name.description: The profile's name as the console showed it when the host chose it.

owner.description:
The host confirmed this profile although it is their own (the one in front): the guest can
use its saves and trophies. Without it the helper refuses that profile.

"Guests play as": the console profile a guest on Player `player` gets, chosen by the host for
one console (user ids are that console's). The helper seats the guest's pad in it as it is made
(`vpad.open` with `bind_user`), so the console never asks "Who's using this controller?" and the
guest cannot pick another profile. No entry for a player: the console asks (as before).

The host confirmed this profile although it is their own (the one in front): the guest can
use its saves and trophies. Without it the helper refuses that profile.

SessionInfo.description:
The running session as a stream for a site sees it (Go live checks it against each site's
limits, rp_golive.rs).

libraries.description: library name -> sha256 of the build this set ships.

observations.description:
Every sighting of this set, oldest first. Absent on corpora written
before observations existed, which is why it defaults rather than
forcing a schema bump: bumping would make every existing corpus read as
empty and silently discard the user's library sets.

allow_permanent_delete.description:

"Guests play as": the profile for each guest's player on `addr` (`{player: 2-4, user,
name, owner}`), replacing the last; empty: the TV asks every guest.

invites.description: "Invites work": "anywhere" or "wifi" (the same choice as `internet_invites`; this one wins).

trash_available.description:
Whether this engine can move files to a trash (false in Docker or on a headless server,
where `allow_permanent_delete` decides).

dest.description: The folder to put things in (default: the Collection's first folder's `Received`).

folder.description: The save folder (every image of it).

image.description: One image (an app before 10.6.0): its whole folder is shared.

expires_in_s.description: Seconds the link works (default 24 h; 60 s to 7 days).

from.description: The sender's name as the friend sees it.

title.description: The game or app the share is about.

ShareItemSpec.description: One thing to share, as the app's page names it.

console.description: The console it is on (an app folder, a save, screenshots, a cheat file).

data.description: Data items: controls, stream settings, which cheats are on.

folder.description: A save folder on the console.

name.description: What the friend sees (the engine names it when left out).

path.description: A path: on the console when `console` is given, else on this computer.

name.description: This side's name as the sender sees it.

any_device.description: Any device on the network may fetch it, not only the console it was made for.

session_id.description: Keeps `cd` and the environment across calls.

Side.description: Which side a handoff is for: the console page (Show on TV) or the PC app (Show on PC).

err.description:
Sentinel for known failure modes — currently the only one is
`pthread_create_failed`. Empty string on success.

poll_seconds.description:
Post-clamp interval. Present even on failure, set to the
current stored value so the UI never shows a stale slider
after a rejected change.

SmpMetaControlReq.description:
SMP-meta worker control. Wraps `smp_meta_control` in spawn_blocking
because the underlying Connection is sync TCP. The `addr` field on
the request body is optional — falls back to the engine's default
PS5 addr — keeping the route shape consistent with the rest of the
/api/ps5/* surface.

action.description:
One of "start", "run_now", "set_poll". Anything else is a no-op.
`start` is idempotent — subsequent calls are silently ignored
inside the payload (the worker only launches once per payload
lifetime).

interval.description:
Required when `action == "set_poll"`; ignored otherwise.
Payload clamps to [5, 600] and returns the post-clamp value in
the ACK so the desktop slider can reconcile.

last_missing.description:
TITLE_ID of the most recent game whose icon0.png couldn't be
located in either sce_sys/ or the bare app root. Empty when
everything healed cleanly.

last_run_unix.description: Unix seconds. 0 means "no sweep has completed yet".

SmpMountedImage.description: One mounted-image row, surfaced in the Library tab's SMP panel.

derived_name.description:
Best-effort image source filename, derived from the mount
point name. SMP doesn't expose the original .ffpkg path
through any read-only surface, so we strip the trailing
"_<8-hex>" hash. Empty if the mount point doesn't match the
expected pattern.

mount_point.description:
Mount point under /mnt/shadowmnt (hashed name SMP picks per
image — `<image_name>_<crc32hex>`).

SmpStatus.description:
Full SMP status snapshot. Every field is null/empty when SMP
isn't present — UI checks `installed` and `running` to decide
what to show.

autotune_ini.description:
Raw autotune.ini — kstuff per-game delays SMP learned from
crash patterns + per-image sector-size overrides.

config_ini.description:
Raw config.ini contents (truncated to READ_LIMIT_BYTES).
Renderer parses + displays as a key/value table; we don't
parse here so the renderer can show the raw file too.

debug_log_tail.description:
Tail of debug.log (last READ_LIMIT_BYTES). Useful for "why
didn't my game mount?" troubleshooting without making the
user FTP into the console.

errors.description:
Per-call error captures. Always present so the renderer can
surface "config.ini exists but couldn't be read" without
inferring from null fields.

installed.description:
True when `/data/shadowmount/debug.log` exists. Implies SMP
has been loaded at least once on this console.

mounted_images.description:
Images currently mounted under /mnt/shadowmnt/. Empty list
when no mounts (or when SMP isn't running). UI shows count.

running.description:
True when a process matching `shadowmountplus` is in PROC_LIST.
Independent of `installed`: SMP can be installed but not
currently running (e.g. user removed it from autoload).

version.description:
SMP's own version (e.g. "1.7beta11") from its HTTP API; `None` when the API does not
answer (older than 1.7beta8, bound to the console only, or switched off).

Source.description:
The request's `source` object: exactly one variant. Externally tagged
(serde default) over a one-field object gives exactly-one-variant
semantics and rejects `{}`.

SpaceRefusal.description:
Why an upload does not fit, as figures: the client words it in the user's language. `Display`
is the English text, which is what the engine logs.

avail_bytes.description: What it may allocate: free space less the margin and other uploads' promises.

image.description: The destination is inside an attached disk image.

late.description:
The console ran out of room after this check had admitted the job; the figures are the
ones it was admitted on.

need_bytes.description: What this upload must still allocate, after crediting the console's copy.

promised_bytes.description: Promised to other uploads running now, already taken off `avail_bytes`.

reused_bytes.description: Already on the console and reused.

volume.description: What the message calls the drive: the destination asked about, or its mount path.

head.description:
Metadata parsed from `parts[0]` (the only part with the PKG
header). Fields like `title` / `icon` come from the lead file.

part_sizes.description: Per-part sizes in bytes (same order as `parts`).

action.description: `off`: stop indexing the drive and remove its index. `remove_index`: remove the old index.

has_index.description: An old index (`.Spotlight-V100`) is on the drive.

StartBody.description: No Debug: it can carry keys.

user.description:
Which PS5 user to play as, when the console has more than one paired: an account id, a name
as `GET /api/consoles` lists it under `rp_users` (any case), or its number there (1, 2, …).
Left out, the chosen user: the one picked last in Play, else the last paired. The console
signs that user in when the session starts. A session already running for the console as
another user answers 409 `busy_user`: stop it first.

action.description:
Echo of the action we requested. Lets the renderer match an
ACK to a pending request without tracking trace IDs.

code.description: Sony API error code (when `err` is set).

err.description:
Sony API error string for the non-destructive `tick` path,
or `standby_unavailable` when dlsym failed.

ok.description:
True when the Sony API call returned success (or, for the
destructive actions, when our pre-call ACK landed).

deep.description:
Also a real 4 KiB direct send into a probe folder: catches a forward that reaches
another console than the one meant (its key does not match).

ntp_server.description:
Optional custom NTP server. Defaults to Cloudflare → Google →
pool.ntp.org → Windows (first success wins).

target_unix_seconds.description:
Target wall-clock time as unix seconds (UTC). Required when
`use_ntp` is false (or absent): a missing one is a 400, never a
clock set to 1970. Ignored when `use_ntp` is true, so an NTP sync
may omit it entirely.

use_ntp.description:
When true, the engine queries an NTP server (Cloudflare/Google/
pool.ntp.org) for the current time instead of using the client-
provided `target_unix_seconds`. This avoids PC-clock drift and
is the recommended mode for accurate time sync.

ntp_server.description: Which NTP server answered. None when `source` is "client".

ok.description:
Raw payload-reported `ok` field. Note `ok: true` doesn't mean
the clock moved — see `stub_no_op` for the detection.

reason.description: Short, user-readable reason for the err_code. Empty when ok.

stub_no_op.description:
True when the payload reported `ok` but the post-set unix is
still >5s away from the requested target. Indicates the SDK
stub returned success without actually touching the clock.

target_unix.description: The epoch the console was actually asked to adopt.

used_fallback.description:
True when the payload set the clock via `settimeofday` because
the SCE call was unavailable, rejected, or a no-op. Surfaced
because it has a visible consequence: settimeofday moves the
kernel wall clock underneath ShellCore, so Sony's Settings UI
may keep showing the old time until reopened.

ToastBody.description:
GET /api/version — engine self-identification.

Returned shape: `{"version": "x.y.z"}`. Used by the Tauri shell
to detect a version-mismatched sibling engine on the bound port:
if /api/version disagrees with the version the shell was built
against, the shell kills the old engine + respawns its own.
Without this, an upgrade-and-relaunch cycle could leave the shell
talking to the prior version's engine indefinitely (silently
missing any newly-added routes — e.g. the FS_OP frames added in
2.2.7).

Transfer7zReq.description:
`/api/transfer/7z` request. Mirrors `TransferZipReq` minus the per-entry
RAM threshold — 7z streams forward-only with bounded memory, so there's no
inflate-to-RAM-vs-temp knob.

skip_existing.description:
"fast" | "safe": skip files the console already has (the Resume strategy).
Honoured on AVA1 consoles, where the receiver decides; `/api/transfer/dir-reconcile`
sets it when it hands a job to this handler.

unescape_names.description:
The folder was downloaded with `escape_names`: each file goes to the console under the
exact name its kept name stands for (`ps5upload_core::host_names`, #729).

addr.description: The console (a `:port` suffix from an older client is ignored).

dest_dir.description:
Local directory the download lands inside. The remote
basename is appended underneath this — so `dest_dir=/tmp/x`
with `src_path=/data/foo` produces `/tmp/x/foo` (file or
folder, mirroring the upload "one folder per title" rule).

escape_names.description:
When true, a console name this computer can't hold (`a\b`, `a:b`, `CON`) is written
under its reversible form (`ps5upload_core::host_names`) instead of refused; an upload
with `unescape_names` puts it back exactly. The saves code's downloads (#729).

kind.description:
"file" or "folder". The caller already knows from context
(Library/FileSystem row) so we trust the hint and skip a
stat round-trip just to classify.

src_path.description:
Path on the PS5 to download. For `kind: "folder"` this is the
root of the tree; for `kind: "file"` it's the file itself.

unsafe_read.description:
When true, bypasses the payload's writable-root allowlist so system
files (/system/, /system_data/, /system_ex/) can be downloaded.
Read-only — the payload ignores this flag for destructive ops.

compression.description:
"stored" (default: resumes mid-entry after a dropped connection) or "deflate"
(smaller for text-heavy trees; cannot resume, so a drop restarts the archive).

dest_zip.description: Absolute host path of the `.zip` to create (the user-picked save path).

existing.description:
What to do with a file already at `dest_zip`: `replace` overwrites it (the person chose
that, say in a save dialog). Absent: refuse with a 409, as the link download does.

src_path.description: Remote file or folder to archive.

unsafe_read.description:
When true, allows reading files outside the normal payload path
allow-list (e.g. /system, /system_data). Read-only. Default false.

bandwidth_cap_mbps.description:
Per-job bandwidth cap in MB/s. None = use the engine's
default (env-var-controlled). 0 also = no cap.

TransferRarReq.description:
`/api/transfer/rar` request. Like 7z plus an optional `password` for
encrypted archives. (RAR is desktop-only — the phone builds cfg out both
the real handler and this struct, so it lives behind the same gate.)

TransferTarReq.description:
`/api/transfer/tar` request: a tar (`.tar`, `.tar.zst`/`.tzst`, `.tar.gz`/`.tgz`,
`.tar.xz`/`.txz`, `.tar.bz2`/`.tbz2`/`.tbz`) or a lone `.zst`. The same fields as 7z.

TransferZipReq.description:
Upload a `.zip`'s contents, decompressing on the host so files land
already extracted on the PS5. Same shape as `TransferDirReq` but the
source is an archive path instead of a directory.

parts.description:
The copy's other files (a split package's later parts, a `.rar` set's later volumes):
they go with it.

available.description: False when the copies cannot be removed here (no trash, and permanent delete is off).

allow_deletes.description: Let a held-back mass delete through this link run (instead of unlinking).

auto_update.description:
"Keep payloads up to date": check at start and daily, and apply what is newer. Off
unless the user turns it on.

Volume.description:
One entry in the payload's volume list.

Fields mirror `struct statfs` on PS5 FreeBSD: `fs_type` is the short
filesystem name (`ufs`, `bfs`, `nullfs`, `tmpfs`, …), `writable`
reflects the mount's `MNT_RDONLY` flag, `*_bytes` are derived from
block counts, and `mount_from` is the device / pseudo source
(`/dev/nvme1`, `/dev/ssd0.user`, `tmpfs`, ...).

`is_placeholder` is true for PS5 mount slots that have no real drive
attached (tmpfs or <256 MiB). UIs typically filter these out by
default but can show them to reflect hot-plug state.

allocatable_bytes.description:
Bytes considered safe for a new allocation after the reserve above.
This is advisory telemetry; callers should use `allocatable_bytes()` so
responses from older payloads remain safe too.

likely_fits_bytes.description:
How much new data is likely to fit (see `likely_fits_bytes()`). Filled in by the engine
for the app; a payload never sends it.

safety_reserve_bytes.description:
Capacity intentionally held back by the payload. New payloads publish
this; older payloads omit it and the engine derives the same value from
the mount identity via `safety_reserve_bytes()`.

source_image.description:
For mounts under `/mnt/ps5upload/` this is the backing image file
(`/data/homebrew/image.exfat`, etc.), recorded by the payload
when the mount was created. Empty string for non-ours mounts or
for mounts created before this tracking was added. UIs use this
to surface "what file is mounted here" without needing to ask
a different API.

WrappedGameHint.description: A game found one level down inside an otherwise-empty wrapper folder.

ZipInspect.description:
Lightweight preview of a `.zip` for the Upload screen: how much it expands
to, how many files, and the game it contains (if it carries a
`sce_sys/param.json`). Reads only the central directory plus, at most, one
small `param.json` — never inflates the bulk of the archive.

compressed_size.description: Size of the `.zip` on disk — what the user is storing.

entry_names.description:
The archive's file paths (directories left out), in archive order, so
the client can tell a game or package archive from one the user means
to send as it is (#645). At most `ENTRY_NAMES_MAX`; `None` from an
engine that did not list them.

entry_names_complete.description: True when `entry_names` holds every file in the archive.

file_count.description: Number of extractable file entries (directories excluded).

game_root.description:
The path *inside the zip* that contains `sce_sys/` (the game root),
e.g. "MyGame" for `MyGame/sce_sys/param.json`, or "" if param.json is
at the archive root. `None` when no game metadata was found.

title.description: Game title from an embedded `sce_sys/param.json`, if any.

total_uncompressed.description: Sum of uncompressed sizes — what lands on the PS5.

next_set_number.description:
Next set number to hand out. Persisted rather than derived from the
highest live set, because deleting the newest set would otherwise let
the next one reuse its id — and a backport record refers to a set by id,
so reuse would point an undo at unrelated libraries.

state.description:
`queued` (waiting its turn), `running`, `ok`, `problems`, `failed` (could not be
checked at all: `error` says why) or `cancelled`.

complete.description: False until the last folder is done: a backup cut short says so.

console.description: The PS5 it was made on (its host-id), if it said: saves open only on that one.

engine.console_backup.Outcome.description: What became of one folder or save.

item.description: The console path, or a game's title id.

result.description: `done`, `failed`, or `needs_save`: that user has no save of the game to put it in yet.

users.description: For saves: the user number in the backup to the user here it goes to.

pid.description: The elfldr running afterwards, when known.

output_dir.description:
Where the package would go; defaults to `~/Downloads/fpkgs`. Used only to report
the room left.

source.description: A game folder, or a `.exfat` / `.ffpkg` / `.ffpfsc` mount image.

update.description:
A PS4 update to look at merged into the game `source` (see `ps5upload_fpkg::ps4_merge`):
the answer is the merged game's, or why the two don't go together.

confirmed.description:
The caller accepts that storing into an existing `ps5upload` folder removes its other
files (Payload Manager's own rule).

console.description: Check `hub` on this other console instead (linking a drive to it).

drive.description: Checked for this drive (joining it): its own folders are not "taken".

hub.description: The console folder (or the folder a new one goes in, with `hub_name`).

engine.net_doctor.LinkKind.description: What kind of link carries the traffic.

The caller saw `check`'s answer and accepts that storing into an existing folder
removes that folder's other files.

filename.description: The name Payload Manager files it under (its folder is derived from this).

local_path.description: A file on this computer (the catalogue's cached ELF).

position.description: Among the console's waiting items, from 0. Left out, the end of the line.

request.description: The body of the kind's route. Its console is this item's.

stop_on_failure.description: If this item fails, the ones after it are paused for someone to look at.

engine.rp_stream_api.Secret.description: A passcode as the page sent it: never printed, not even in a debug dump.

engine.rp_stream_api.control.PasscodeReq.description: No Debug: it carries the passcode.

picture.description: The picture on the attached page on or off (see rp_stream_api's module note).

save_path.description: The save folder on the console (from the saves list).

add_hosts.description:
Consoles to add to `hosts`, whatever else is on it: what a client knows of its own roster.
Several clients share one engine, so none of them sends the whole list.

addr.description: The console's tailnet address or MagicDNS name (as found, or typed).

name.description: A name for a new entry; its tailnet name otherwise.

engine.wake_login_api.Secret.description: A passcode as the client sent it: never printed, not even in a debug dump.

get.description:
`GET /api/ava1/console?addr=` — who answers at this address: the console's AVA1 key (hex,
its identity at every address) and the name it gives. Read from the first two handshake
messages only (`peek_console`): the console never admits, pairs or lists this device for it,

get.description:
`GET /api/tailnet/consoles[?refresh=1&all=1&addr=]` — the PS5Upload consoles on this device's
Tailscale network: `{ok, backend, can_list, cached, age_ms, consoles: [{name, tailnet_name,
tailnet_ip, lan_host, id, reachable, via, online, paired, hosts, listed, error}]}`.

* `backend`: how this device is on Tailscale (`builtin`, `system`, `none`). `can_list`: whether
  a peer list could be read (false on a phone with only the system Tailscale app: type the
  address instead, `addr=`).
* Each console was asked on TCP 9120 through Tailscale: `reachable` when its helper answered,
  `id` its AVA1 key (hex, the same at every address), `via` `builtin` or `system`, `error`
  why not. Nothing is paired or pinned by asking, and no code shows on the PS5.
* `lan_host`: its home address when this engine knows one; `hosts` every address it was met
  at; `listed`: the console list's entry for it (`{id, name, host}`) or null; `paired`: this
  engine is trusted by it already.
* `addr=` probes that one address now (a 100.x address or a MagicDNS name) and answers
  `{ok, console: {...}}`; 400 `not_tailnet` when it is neither.

Answered from the last minute's look unless `refresh=1`; nothing is looked for in the
background.

post.description:
`POST /api/tailnet/consoles/add` `{addr, name?}` — puts a console found on Tailscale (or typed:
a 100.x address or a MagicDNS name) on the console list, probing it first. Answers `{ok,
action, console: {id, name, host}, found: {...the list entry...}}`; `action` is `added`,
`linked` (its entry at the tailnet address moved to its home address), `merged` (two entries
for it became one) or `exists`.

One entry per console: at its home address when one is known (so the home network is used
when back home, Tailscale when away), else at its tailnet address, which becomes the home
one when the console is next reached at home. Either way its tailnet address is remembered
for the router. A console that does not answer is still added (its list may not let this
device in yet: the PS5 then shows "tried to reach this PS5" with Allow).

post.description:
POST /api/zip/inspect/stream — same shape as `/api/zip/inspect` but
returns an `Sse` response so the client can render progress and the
connection can survive a slow cold-cache central-directory read.

**Why streaming instead of just the long-deadline `/api/zip/inspect`:**
even after Phase 2 (zero-seek CD parser) cut warm inspect to ~35 ms,
pathological cases (network mount, spun-down USB HDD, very large
zips with 100k+ entries) can still take several seconds. The user
reported "engine request failed: error sending request" was the
short-deadline (60 s) timer firing on the old per-entry-seek
pipeline; with this endpoint the client uses a dead-man-switch
watchdog instead — "no chunk for N seconds" — and shows live entry
counts during the wait. The handler emits three event types:

- `progress` — `{"entries_seen": N}` periodically while the central
  directory is being walked. Drives the UI "Scanning archive… N
  entries" indicator and resets the client watchdog.
- `done` — `{...ZipInspect...}` once. Final event; client closes
  the connection on receipt.
- `error` — `{"error": "..."}` once. Final event on a parse / IO
  failure. The HTTP status stays 200 because headers ship before
  the worker knows whether inspect will succeed; this matches
  `events_stream` (the existing SSE precedent in this engine).

`KeepAlive::interval(1s)` makes axum send an SSE comment line every
second when no real event is in flight, so the client's watchdog
sees forward motion even during a CD bulk-read that emits no
progress callbacks. The 1 s cadence is short enough to keep the UI
"Scanning…" indicator responsive without flooding the channel.
